'''Lin Ming-chang''' ({{lang-zh|c=林明璋|p=Lín Míngzhāng}}; born 24 October 1936) is a Taiwanese chemist.

== Life and career ==
Born in Zhaomen, [[Xinpu, Hsinchu]], on 24 October 1936, Lin Ming-chang attended [[Hsinchu Senior High School]] and graduated from [[National Taiwan Normal University]] before pursuing graduate study under [[Keith J. Laidler]] at the [[University of Ottawa]]. After completing his postdoctoral research in Ottawa, Lin joined Simon H. Bauer at [[Cornell University]] in 1967. Lin moved to the [[United States Naval Research Laboratory]] in 1970.<ref name="journalbio">{{cite journal |last1=Bowman |first1=JM |last2=Heaven |first2=MC |last3=Lee |first3=YP |title=Biography of Ming-Chang Lin |journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry |date=26 July 2007 |volume=3 |issue=29 |pages=6569–71 |doi=10.1021/jp079523k |pmid=17637036 |bibcode=2007JPCA..111.6569. |url=http://chemistry.emory.edu/faculty/lin/mclin-bio.pdf |accessdate=2 December 2018 }}</ref><ref name="rocyb">{{cite book |title=The Republic of China Yearbook |date=2010 |publisher=Government Information Office |page=427 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EnAmDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA427 |accessdate=2 December 2018|isbn=9789860252781 }}</ref>

While working at the NRL, Lin received a [[Navy Meritorious Civilian Service Award]] in 1979, followed by a [[Guggenheim fellowship]] and [[Alexander von Humboldt Award]] in 1982.<ref name="jphyschemb">{{cite journal |title=Alexander-von-Humboldt-Stiftung − Awardees and Fellows of Gerhard Ertl |journal=J. Phys. Chem. B |date=16 September 2004 |volume=108 |issue=38 |pages=14193–14194 |doi=10.1021/jp0404100 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Ming-chang Lin |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/ming-chang-lin/ |accessdate=2 December 2018 |publisher=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation}}</ref> From 1981, Lin concurrently held an adjunct professorship at the [[Catholic University of America]].<ref name="rocyb" /> in 1988, he became Robert W. Woodruff Professor of Chemistry at [[Emory University]]. In 2000, he became a member of [[Academia Sinica]].<ref name="nctu" />

Lin was named TSMC Distinguished Professor at [[National Chiao Tung University]] in 2005, where he had served as director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Molecular Science since 2002.<ref name="rocyb" /> In 2009, Lin was named a foreign fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry.<ref name="nctu">{{cite news |title=Ming-Chang Lin |url=http://www.ac.nctu.edu.tw/en/member/Ming-Chang-Lin-12010680 |accessdate=2 December 2018 |publisher=National Chiao Tung University}}</ref> Lin retired from NCTU in 2011, and was granted distinguished professor emeritus status.<ref name="rocyb" />

Lin supported [[Tsai Ing-wen]]'s 2012 presidential campaign.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Chang |first1=Rich |title=2012 ELECTIONS: TSU throws its support behind DPP |url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2011/12/26/2003521640 |accessdate=2 December 2018 |work=Taipei Times |date=26 December 2011}}</ref> Lin backed efforts to end nuclear power production in Taiwan, submitting a petition advising people to vote against question ten of the [[2018 Taiwanese referendum]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maxon |first1=Ann |title=2018 ELECTIONS: Group warns against nuclear bid |url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2018/11/15/2003704266 |accessdate=2 December 2018 |work=Taipei Times |date=15 November 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Lin |first1=Rachel |title=Academics push petition against key referendum |url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2018/11/05/2003703619 |accessdate=2 December 2018 |work=Taipei Times |date=5 November 2018}}</ref>
